                                                                  Abstract                                       (a) Task: "How to turn on incognito mode on Google Maps?"


                                         Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs)
                                         and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have sparked signifi-
                                         cant interest in developing GUI visual agents. We introduce
                                         MONDAY (Mobile OS Navigation Task Dataset for Agents
                                         from YouTube), a large-scale dataset of 313K annotated
                                         frames from 20K instructional videos capturing diverse
                                                                                                                  (b) iOS example screens          (c) Android example screens
                                         real-world mobile OS navigation across multiple platforms.
                                         Models that include MONDAY in their pre-training phases
                                         demonstrate robust cross-platform generalization capabili-
                                         ties, consistently outperforming models trained on existing
                                         single OS datasets while achieving an average performance
                                         gain of 18.11%p on an unseen mobile OS platform. To
                                         enable continuous dataset expansion as mobile platforms
                                         evolve, we present an automated framework that leverages
                                         publicly available video content to create comprehensive
                                         task datasets without manual annotation. Our framework
                                         comprises robust OCR-based scene detection (95.04% F1-                Figure 1. Example screens from our MONDAY dataset: (a) mobile
                                         score), near-perfect UI element detection (99.87% hit ra-             OS navigation sequence showing how to turn off incognito mode
                                         tio), and novel multi-step action identification to extract re-       on Google Maps. Our dataset captures real-world mobile OS nav-
                                         liable action sequences across diverse interface configura-           igation procedures across different platforms and configurations,
                                         tions. We contribute both the MONDAY dataset and our au-              enabling effective generalization; (b) iOS interfaces across differ-
                                         tomated collection framework to facilitate future research            ent versions and user configurations, including light/dark mode,
                                                                                                               custom control center, and accessibility settings; (c) Android inter-
                                         in mobile OS navigation.
                                                                                                               faces with various themes, app layouts, and different resolutions.

                                                                                                                  A fundamental technical challenge in developing robust
                                         agents have increasingly succeeded in executing natural lan-
                                                                                                               mobile OS navigation agents lies in acquiring diverse, real-
                                         guage instructions on GUI systems, including mobile oper-
                                                                                                               world training data that reflects the wide variety of UI lay-
                                         ating systems (OS), using only visual cues [8, 54]. These
                                                                                                               outs, elements, and interactions that users encounter in prac-
                                         agents enable hands-free device control, which is particu-
                                                                                                               tice. Existing approaches [8, 54] rely heavily on datasets
                                         larly valuable for users with physical limitations or in situa-
                                                                                                               that capture device control through manually annotated
                                         tions where manual interaction is impractical. Such agents

tional videos. In this section, we first describe the dataset          evolve. A detailed analysis of computational requirements
characteristics and key properties, followed by our auto-              and costs is provided in Supplementary Section A.
mated framework for data collection and annotation.

                                                                                                             C. Details about MONDAY Framework
Figure C. Filtering stages in video collection process. Starting                                             Our framework, illustrated in Figure 2, consists of three
from 129K YouTube videos with English transcripts and duration                                               main components working together to extract mobile OS
under 15 minutes, each stage progressively filters videos to ensure                                          navigation procedures from instructional videos. The

H. Expanded Related Work                                             I. Episode Examples
H.1. Cross-Domain GUI Datasets and Approaches                        We present example episodes from our dataset to demon-
                                                                     strate the effectiveness of our action identification frame-
Early GUI agent benchmarks often focused on simple,                  work. The examples are organized into three categories:
single-step tasks or were confined to a single platform, lim-        perfectly identified sequences, near-miss cases with mul-
iting cross-environment generalization [44]. Recently, there         tiple valid action paths, and challenging cases involving
have been efforts to scale up data collection for web and            platform-specific operations. Figures G and H showcase
GUI-based environments to support the training of agents             successful action identification sequences on Android and
on a wider range of computer interaction tasks. Agent-               iOS platforms, respectively. In these examples, our frame-
Trek [50] simulates actions in a virtual environment based           work correctly identifies all user interactions, demonstrat-
on tutorial text, with step-by-step instructions from GPT-           ing its robustness across different mobile operating systems.
4o. WebArena [56] offers a high-fidelity browser simulation          Figures I and J illustrate cases where multiple valid interac-
with complex, long-horizon web tasks. Mind2Web [10] col-             tion paths exist. Our framework typically selects the most
lects crowdsourced demonstrations on real-world websites,            direct path to accomplish the task, though this may occa-
though data collection is expensive and limited to web do-           sionally differ from human demonstrations. Figures K and
mains. GUI-World [5] spans multiple platforms (web, mo-              L present challenging scenarios involving platform-specific
bile, desktop), but is restricted to question-answering rather       operations or security features. These examples highlight
than full action-based tasks.                                        current limitations in handling specialized interactions like
    While simulator-based approaches in web and computer             secure input or complex scrolling patterns.
OS domains can extend to Android via emulators, iOS’s
closed APIs hinder automated interaction extraction, limit-
ing multi-platform coverage. MONDAY avoids direct GUI
access by leveraging YouTube videos and automatically de-
tecting scenes and actions. Unlike simulators, which pro-
vide built-in interaction logs, MONDAY tackles data ex-
traction using OCR-based scene segmentation, UI detection
via GroundingDINO, and a three-step action identification
pipeline. This approach is also adaptable to web and desk-
top GUIs, although higher resolutions and complex interac-
tions may introduce new challenges.
